sections.h2: Which Arkansas laws cover landlords and tenants?
sections.html:
The main statute is the Arkansas Residential Landlord-Tenant Act of 2007, found in Chapter 17 of Title 18 of the Arkansas Code. The Attorney General adds that these rules apply to private rental units and not to government-subsidized housing.

Legal Aid of Arkansas describes the Act as a law meant to simplify and modernize residential rental rules. It sets out what a rental agreement may contain, such as rent and the length of the term, and the steps to follow when either side breaks the agreement. Some living arrangements fall outside it. Section 18-17-202 lists them, and Legal Aid names institutional residences for medical, educational or religious services, stays in hotels and motels that are subject to sales tax, and protective shelters.

The Act also puts duties on the renter. Section 18-17-601 requires a tenant to follow housing codes that affect health and safety, keep the unit clean and safe, dispose of waste in a reasonable way and keep plumbing fixtures reasonably clean. The Attorney General notes that both oral and written leases bind the parties, though a written lease avoids arguments about who promised what.

sections.h2: How do Arkansas security deposit rules work?
sections.html:
Arkansas caps a deposit at two months' rent, but only for landlords who rent six or more dwellings. The table shows the main points from the Attorney General and Legal Aid of Arkansas.

QuestionAnswerSource
Who is covered?Landlords who rent six or more dwellings; Legal Aid also counts a landlord who has someone manage or collect rentAttorney General; Legal Aid
Maximum depositTwo months' rentAttorney General
Deadline to return it60 days after the tenant moves outAttorney General
If money is keptA written, itemized list of charges within 60 days of vacatingAttorney General
Can the landlord keep it all?Yes, when damage or unpaid rent exceeds the depositAttorney General
If the landlord ignores the rulesThe tenant may be owed twice the deposit plus costs and attorney's feesLegal Aid

A landlord with five or fewer properties falls outside these provisions, Legal Aid says. In that case the written lease matters even more, and a tenant can still sue in small claims court for the deposit, where the landlord may counterclaim for unpaid rent or damage. Legal Aid also says that if a landlord cannot find the former tenant after a reasonable attempt, the landlord may keep the whole deposit after 180 days.

sections.h2: What notice does a landlord owe for rent increases and lease endings?
sections.html:
A landlord must give notice of at least one rental period before raising the rent, on oral and written leases alike. The Attorney General also says a landlord may end a lease for any reason, with one rental period's notice on an oral lease or the notice the written lease calls for.

  • A tenant who wants to sublease usually needs the landlord's approval first, plus written direction on how much rent can be collected.
  • A tenant leaving a written lease follows the lease's notice terms, and a tenant leaving an oral lease gives one rental period's notice.
  • Under the Act, a week-to-week tenancy ends on seven days' written notice and a month-to-month tenancy on 30 days' written notice, from either side (§ 18-17-704).

Legal Aid adds that a landlord who declines to renew may do so for any reason except those the Fair Housing Act forbids.

sections.h2: Who has to make repairs in an Arkansas rental?
sections.html:
It depends on when the lease was signed. The Attorney General's guidance says renters usually take a house or apartment as is, and a landlord is not required to provide extra maintenance beyond what city building codes demand. Any promised repair should be written into the lease. A tenant should keep paying rent even if a promised repair is not done, and the Attorney General points to small claims court, renegotiating, moving out or a private attorney as recourse.

A 2021 law changed the picture for newer leases. Under § 18-17-502, leases signed or renewed after November 1, 2021 carry implied standards for a dwelling or single-family house: running hot and cold water, electricity, drinking water, a sanitary sewer and plumbing that meet code, a functioning roof and building envelope, and heating and air conditioning if the home had them at lease signing.

The statute has some safe harbors for landlords. A landlord is treated as compliant if the tenant is handed a written defect form at move-in and either signs it without listing a defect or fails to return it within two business days. Defects caused by the tenant, the tenant's family or visitors do not count against the landlord. A tenant can install a battery-powered or plug-in smoke or carbon monoxide detector at personal expense, and then becomes responsible for keeping it working. A city or county with stricter housing standards still applies its own rules.

sections.h2: What can a landlord do when a tenant breaks the lease?
sections.html:
The landlord's first tool is written notice. Section 18-17-701 allows a notice that names the acts or omissions and says the agreement will end at least 14 days after receipt unless the problem is fixed. Unpaid rent works faster: if rent is not paid within five days of the due date, the landlord may terminate.

A tenant who refuses lawful access can be ordered by a district court to allow it, since § 18-17-705 lets the landlord seek an injunction. A landlord may recover actual damages and, when represented by a lawyer, attorney's fees if nonpayment was not in good faith. The full eviction steps, from the three-day unlawful detainer notice to the sheriff's writ, are laid out on our Arkansas eviction process page.

sections.h2: What does the Fair Housing Act add?
sections.html:
It bars discrimination in renting or selling a dwelling based on race, color, religion, gender, handicap, familial status or national origin. The Attorney General lists several specific bans.

  • Advertisements that signal a preference or limit, such as adults-only for part of a complex.
  • Different terms or conditions of sale or rent.
  • Discrimination in the use of facilities tied to the dwelling.
  • Assigning a person to a particular section of a complex or a particular floor.

Complaints can go to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development or the Arkansas Fair Housing Commission.

sections.h2: How does selling a rental house change these rules?
sections.html:
Selling does not end the duties above on its own. The statutes cited here speak to the landlord and the tenant, and none of them says a sale cancels a lease, so the lease terms and an attorney's advice should come first.

Owners considering a sale usually weigh a few facts. A month-to-month tenant can be given 30 days' written notice, and a landlord who will not renew needs a lawful reason, which in Arkansas can be any reason that is not discriminatory. The deposit is a separate matter: ask the closing attorney how the deposit and any prepaid rent will be handled so the tenant's refund rights are not left hanging.

A rented house also changes tax paperwork. The Assessment Coordination Division asks owners to notify the assessor when a house goes from owner-occupied to rental, and the transfer tax of $3.30 per $1,000 of consideration applies to the deed. In Little Rock, privately owned rentals with two or more dwellings must meet the city's minimum housing standards, which include working plumbing, electricity and a roof that does not leak.

sections.h2: Where can landlords and tenants get help in Arkansas?
sections.html: Legal Aid of Arkansas runs a landlord and tenant guide and a free helpline at 1-800-952-9243 for people who qualify. The Attorney General's page also points to the Arkansas Community Action Agencies. In Little Rock, the Department of Housing and Neighborhood Programs takes housing code complaints at (501) 371-6825, and residents can call 211 for utility and housing help.

faqs.q: What is the maximum security deposit in Arkansas?
faqs.a: Two months' rent. The cap applies to landlords who rent six or more dwellings, so a landlord with fewer properties is not bound by that statute, though the lease still controls.

faqs.q: How long does a landlord have to return a deposit in Arkansas?
faqs.a: Sixty days after the tenant moves out. A landlord who deducts must send a written, itemized list of charges within the same 60 days, according to the Attorney General.

faqs.q: Can an Arkansas landlord raise the rent whenever they want?
faqs.a: No. The landlord must give notice of at least one rental period before raising rent, whether the lease is oral or written. Check the lease for any terms about rent during a fixed term.

faqs.q: Does a tenant have to keep paying rent if the landlord skips a repair?
faqs.a: Yes. Section 18-17-502 says a tenant may not withhold or offset rent over implied quality standards. After written notice and 30 calendar days with rent current, the tenant's sole remedy is to end the lease without penalty and recover a deposit that is owed.

faqs.q: Do these laws cover subsidized housing?
faqs.a: No. The Attorney General states that Arkansas landlord and tenant laws apply only to private rental units, not government-subsidized housing.

faqs.q: Can a landlord end a lease so the owner can sell?
faqs.a: The Attorney General says a landlord may end a lease for any reason with the required notice. The sources do not list a sale as a special ground, so a lawyer should confirm the notice period for your lease before you send it.
